## **Backstory**

* **Personal Backstory (The full details of their past):**  
  Syrena is the 11th child out of 24, of an infamous Dragonborn noble from Aries city. She never knew her biological mother. None of her half siblings do, each one had a different mother so the house was filled with children of diverse mixed races. Syrena's bastard father was a pervert; she and her siblings assumed that his dozens of wives died from giving birth to them or from suffering his wrath.  
  Growing up, Syrena and her siblings were abused and trained past their limits to become the best experts their own bloodline has to offer because their father was greedy and desperate to build his own empire. He wanted to be the fifth region where he is the only king amongst all kingdoms. There is a hidden motive behind this.  
  She and her siblings despise him. Their childhood was destroyed by his torture and expectations. Their futures were decided and controlled by him. Their father was infamous for being a shitty narcissistic dictator. Even though he didn't rule an empire yet, he was a rich enough noble who owned a single land and controlled everyone living there. He uses all his 24 children to do his bidding and build his empire for him.  
  One day, when his land was attacked by riots (dissatisfied citizens who were treated harshly under his rule), Syrena and a few of her siblings managed to escape but got separated when they were being chased by the rioters.  
  Syrena decided that in order to survive, she wasn't going to give anyone the chance to hurt, control, manipulate and use her like her ugly sperm donor did. Therefore, she releases all her pent up childhood trauma in the form of anger so no one would even think about messing with her. She escaped to Cancer and sought refuge there. But she doesn't stay in one place for too long because her disgusting ass father had been sending assassins to find her. Some of those assassins and mercenaries going after her are her own siblings (those who never got to leave). They are equally as violent and skillfully trained as she is. She needed to earn money for living expenses but the only thing she knew how to do that was to compete in the secret underground fighting rings. That's how she became a Venatrix. She hated fighting, it was what her father expected of her. Ironically, that's the only best asset she currently has to survive on her own. For now. Syrena kept moving from one place to another until she found the group. The main story takes place a few months after she escaped.

# Khalen Moren

## **Details**

* **Name:** Khalen Moren  
* **Age: 22**  
* **Gender/Pronouns:** Male (he/him)  
* **Class:** Wizard  
* **Subclass:** Bladesinger  
* **Race:** Half Elf  
* **Background:** Commoner  
* **Divine Connection (if applicable):**   
* **Familiar (if applicable):** Ignatius – A small, burgundy fire salamander with amber eyes and a turtle-like beak. Standoffish and fiercely intelligent, he spits fire when threatened and shares an empathic bond with Khalen, though the two are still learning to trust one another. 

## **Appearance**

* **Hair:** Shaggy but short brown hair  
* **Eyes:** pale grey-green  
* **Skin:** lightskinned, a light scar along his ribs from the collapse in Innsvale that never fully faded   
* **Build:** Lean but wiry-strong   
* **Height:** Slightly taller than average human, around 5'11  
* **Clothing Style (What do they usually wear?):** A hooded robe/cape, wearing armour that tends to prioritise movement and flexibility than over just raw stopping power

![][image3]

## **Personality**

* **On the Outside (How do others perceive them initially?):** Easygoing, quick with a joke, the kind of person who defuses a tense room rather than adding to it. Comes across as capable, but green, there's an obvious edge of "still figuring this out" to him, whether it's handling a blade in a real fight or trusting his own magic to actually work when it counts. Doesn't talk about his past unless asked, and even then gives you the short version.   
* **On the Inside (What are their true feelings or hidden traits?):** Believes he should have died in Innsvale along with everyone else, and that everything since has been borrowed time he never asked for and doesn't know how to spend. That belief doesn't make him reckless exactly, but it does mean he doesn't fear death the way other people do. Underneath the humor there's mostly grief, sorrow and regret, quiet and constant, worn down enough that it doesn't show most days. He's not chasing glory or coin. He's counting down to a single reckoning, and everything else is just what happens in between.   
* **Quirks:** Flinches slightly at the sound of horns, even friendly ones, hunting horns, festival horns, anything close to the pitch of a warhorn. Recovers fast, but it's there if you're watching for it.   
* **Voice and Mannerisms (Accents, typical gestures, etc.):** Light and quick to joke most of the time, but the second things turn dire, he goes silent, already looking for the way out before the fight's even started. If grief catches him in that same moment, the poem takes over instead of words. People who've traveled with him long enough learn to read both as warning signs.   
* **Daily/Little Habits:** Feeds Ignatius before himself, most days without thinking about it. Takes the watch out and fidgets with it without realizing, opening and closing it over and over, even though it doesn't tell him anything. 

## **Goals and Stakes**

* **Short-term Goals (What do they want to achieve right now?):** Track down anything that points toward the one-eyed orc, a name, a warband, a territory, anything. Figure out what the watch actually does, since it survived the fire untouched for a reason he hasn't puzzled out yet. Keep pace with a group strong enough that he might actually survive long enough to get his reckoning, instead of dying to something meaningless first.   
* **Long-term Goals (What is their ultimate ambition?):** Find the one-eyed orc and end him, personally, by his own hand. Not for the village, not for justice in some abstract sense, just because Khalen watched him kill both his parents without breaking stride and has been carrying that image ever since. He hasn't let himself think much past that moment. Some part of him doesn't expect to need a plan for afterward. Figure out who his father really was. Aldric spent Khalen's whole life playing the quiet village blacksmith, forbidding him from ever touching magic, and then died fighting like he'd done it a thousand times before, with a fortune of elven regalia and magic items buried in a chest no one knew about. That doesn't square with the man Khalen thought he grew up with. Somewhere under the grief there's a real question he can't let go of: what was his father running from, or hiding from, by choosing Innsvale and choosing silence?  
* **Stakes (What do they stand to lose? Who or what is most important to them?):** Ignatius, eventually. Right now the bond is new and uneven, born out of shared terror in a basement, not trust. He doesn't listen to Khalen, doesn't really answer to him, and does his own thing more often than not. But it's the only relationship Khalen has left that started after everything burned, and there's a stubborn part of him that keeps showing up for it anyway, feeding Ignatius first, waiting him out, not forcing anything. If that patience pays off over time, and the two of them actually learn to move as one instead of just tolerating each other, that bond could become the thing Khalen has the most to lose. He just isn't there yet, and neither is Ignatius. 

## 

## 

## **Ignatius**

**Type:** Fire Salamander familiar

**Personality:** Standoffish and independent, especially early on. Doesn't listen to Khalen, doesn't answer to him, does his own thing more often than not. Not cruel, just not bonded through trust yet, the two of them were thrown together by trauma, not choice. Sharp, wary, quick to bite or burn first and figure out the situation second. Fiercely intelligent underneath the wariness.

**Appearance:** About the size of a ferret, low and long, built to lope rather than scuttle. Smooth burgundy skin, almost wine-colored. Large round amber eyes, sharp and alert. No teeth, just a beak-like snout similar to a river turtle's.

**What is he?:** I've never seen anything like him before, not in any of my father's books, not in anything the old traders used to talk about over drinks, not even in the stories the elders told to scare kids into staying close to the village at night. Small as he is, he's not nothing, he spits fire when he's scared, though it's not much more than a spark most days, and there's something sharp behind those eyes that makes me think he understands more than he lets on. But he's still just a scared, scrawny little thing who barely tolerates me. Whatever he actually is under all that, I don't know. My father never mentioned anything like him, not once, and I don't have the first idea where to even start looking for an answer. 

## **Backstory**

* **Personal Backstory (The full details of their past):** 

Innsvale was a human settlement. It wasn't the kind of place you'd expect to find elves at all, let alone one who'd married in and stayed.  It sat right up against the edge of the realm, close enough to the outer planes that on bad nights you could feel it in the air. My father's people spend their long lives chasing power, or knowledge, or something beautiful enough to be worth the chase. He chased none of that, and neither did I. We just wanted quiet, and for a long time, we had it.

My father, Aldric Moren, was a high elf. He was the village blacksmith. It was work beneath what he was capable of, mostly horseshoes and cart wheels and the occasional mended plow, but he never seemed to mind. The village respected him for it. He was the one thing I couldn't figure out growing up, a man clearly capable of more, who chose less, and seemed happy doing it. He also forbade me from ever touching magic. Not angry about it, never raised his voice, just firm in a way that told me the answer wasn't up for discussion. I learned to stop asking before I ever got a reason. 

My mother, Elena Moren, was human, village-born, and never once let anyone forget that Innsvale was as much my fathers home as anyone's. She ran the house, fed whoever showed up hungry, and never once made anyone feel like a burden for needing help. My sister, Isabel, was ten. She spent her days running around with the other village kids, too young to know how thin the ground under us really was.

I was the restless one. Blacksmithing never interested me, and neither did staying put. I wanted to be an adventurer, to see something past the tree line for once, to come home with stories and gold and finally be worth something to the people who'd put up with me for so long. I didn't know yet what that kind of dream actually costs. I found out fast.

A stranger walked into town one morning, the first traveler we'd had in years. Everyone gave him a wide berth, wouldn't even look at him twice. I saw an opening and took it, got him a bed and a hot meal, and it earned me just enough trust to ask him questions over the next few days. He answered some of them. Grudgingly.

Something was wrong with him. He flinched at nothing, kept checking over his shoulder like he expected the room to turn on him. He kept his left side wrapped and never let anyone near it. I caught a glimpse once, by accident, green streaks crawling under his skin like nothing I'd ever seen, and I grew up around people who knew every poison in these woods. Whatever it was, it was killing him slowly, and he was running from something a lot faster than the poison.

A few days later, the horde hit us.

Warhorns first, then arrows, then the gates were just gone and orcs were pouring through them. I didn't run to help anyone. I ran to hide. Every idea I'd ever had about being brave disappeared the second things got real, and I watched people I'd known my whole life get cut down while I stayed pinned in a doorway, doing nothing. Then one of them saw me.

I got cornered by a rider on a war boar and I should have died right there, would have, if an arrow hadn't dropped the boar first. It went down, threw the orc, and I heard its neck snap on the landing. The stranger had loosed the shot. He grabbed my arm and hauled me up before I could even process it.

We were running when I saw my father standing his ground, sword in one hand and, somehow, magic in the other. I had never once seen him cast a spell in my life, and yet there was nothing uncertain about it, no hesitation, no fumbled words, like his hands remembered something the rest of him had spent years pretending to forget. He fought like a man returning to an old habit, not learning a new one. But it wasn't enough. A scarred orc came through the smoke on an armored beast, bigger than the others, moving like he expected the battle to part around him. His tusks were capped in dull iron, chipped from years of use, and old scars crossed his face in a pattern too even to be anything but deliberate, something carved rather than earned in battle. He drove a spear straight through my father's back without breaking stride. My mother went for him and he backhanded a hand axe into her chest without turning to look, like swatting something out of his way. He had one eye. The other was scarred shut, milk-white, long healed over, but he didn't need it to find her. 

I screamed. I wanted to go to them, but Isabel was still out there somewhere. I turned to look for her and caught one glimpse, just far enough away, orcs closing in around where the younger kids had been herded. I ran for her anyway. The stranger physically stopped me, dragging me the other way, and I fought him for it, I actually fought him, until the screaming from that part of the village stopped instantly. The silence was deafening, I couldn't believe what that meant in the moment. The stranger was fading fast by then himself, muttering the same thing under his breath, over and over, *they've found me, they've found me.* I got him into a basement so he could rest while the orcs, apparently not finding whatever they'd actually come for, leveled the village on the one-eyed one's order. The blast sealed the only way out. We were stuck down there while everything I knew burned above us, and I already knew there was nothing left up there worth digging out for. 

We both got worse over the next few days, him a lot faster than me. When he finally died I went through his things, half looking for anything useful, half just needing something to do. That's when I saw the rest of it, the whole left side of him was eaten up by that same green rot, way further gone than I'd realized. It had been killing him long before he ever walked into Innsvale.

Most of what he carried was garbage. But there was a wooden case with markings I didn't recognize, and inside it, just an old scroll, dusty and useless as far as I could tell. I gave up after that. Everyone I loved was dead, I was buried alive in a basement, and I didn't have anything left to fight for, nothing waiting for me even if I did claw my way out. So I lay back and let my eyes close, thinking about a poem my father used to say when I was little: 

In the bleak mid-winter, frosty wind made moan; earth stood hard as iron, water like a stone; snow had fallen, snow on snow, snow on snow, in the bleak mid-winter, long ago.

I was still crying, eyes half shut, ready to let go, and that's when the scroll caught fire. 

Not burned, lit up, throwing sparks into the dark and snapping me back awake. Something came out of the light, about the size of a ferret, built low and long like it was meant to lope instead of scuttle. Deep burgundy skin, almost wine colored. Big round eyes, amber, sharp as anything. No teeth, just a beak like a river turtle's. It looked as scared as I felt, and just as ready to bite something.

That was Ignatius. He didn't like me. Still doesn't, most days. At first he just wanted to burn something, spitting fire at the walls, at me, at nothing, and I didn't blame him. I was scared and half-buried alive too. What finally settled him wasn't anything I did on purpose. I just sat there in the dark with him, shaking, and at some point I realized I could feel what he was feeling, not words, not thoughts, just the raw shape of it, fear on top of fear, echoing back and forth between us with nowhere else to go. He could feel mine the same way. Neither of us had to explain it to the other, because there was nothing to explain, just two things that were terrified in the same hole in the ground, and somehow that was enough to bind to. 

Getting out took the better part of a day. The blast had brought half the house down over the entrance, packed earth and broken beams with no give in them anywhere. I dug where I could reach and Ignatius burned through what I couldn't, scorching the wood down to something brittle enough to break apart by hand. We took turns resting so neither of us collapsed. By the time we broke through to open air I hadn't eaten in days, my hands were raw and blistered from clawing through rubble, and I had a gash along my ribs from a fall I didn't even remember taking. I came up into the light running on nothing.

What we found above ground took my legs out from under me. Nothing but ash and burned timber, farther than I could see. Ignatius scuttled off the second we broke the surface, gone into the wreckage before I even had a chance to call after him, I figured that was the last I'd see of him, and honestly I didn't have it in me to care. My whole life, gone in a night, and I was barely able to stand up to look at it. I found my parents not far from where they'd fallen. There wasn't much dignity left in how they'd died, so I tried to give them some after. I carried them, one at a time, out past the well to the old elm they used to sit under on warm evenings, the one my mother always said she wanted to grow old next to. I dug the grave with my bare hands because I couldn't bring myself to go looking for a shovel in the wreckage.

I found Isabel not far from where the other children had been herded, close enough to the tree line that some part of me thinks she almost made it out. She was small enough that I didn't need to carry her in two trips like I had with our parents. That was the only mercy in any of it. I buried her next to them, under the same elm, and I didn't have anything to say over her grave that felt like enough, so I didn't say anything at all.

I buried anyone else I could find. Then I went to what was left of my house and found the floor caved in around a metal crate, lock already blown off, I don't know what. Inside was elven regalia and a handful of magic items, a wand, some books, all of it totally destroyed. A few books survived. Barely. Everything else in that crate had been through the fire. Warped covers, ash where pages used to be, metal gone black and brittle. But there was a pouch sitting on top of it all, midnight black, a white dragon stitched into the fabric in some kind of metallic thread, and it wasn't touched. Not scorched, not even warm. Inside was a pocket watch, broken, the glass cracked and the hands frozen at some position that meant nothing to me. Where the numbers should have been there were only symbols, and the same strange script wound its way across the casing too, one continuous pattern like the whole thing had been carved as a single piece, nothing like the elven script in the ruined books beside it, older-looking, or maybe just foreign in a way I couldn't place. I didn't know what it did, if it did anything at all, but something about how untouched it was next to everything else told me it mattered. My father, the man who wouldn't let me near a spellbook, had been sitting on a fortune of magic the whole time and never said a word. 

I cried over that too. Grieved a father I apparently never actually knew. There was no one left to grieve for after that, no father, mother or sister, no reason to keep moving except the fact that I was, somehow, still breathing when I shouldn't have been. I should have died with my family. Most days I still think I did, and all of this is just a bad dream.

I took what I could still use out of my father's chest, some minor burned spell books, some tomes, that watch, and the pouch it came in, and went back to the stranger's body, taking anything useful off him, his coat, backpack, and his pieces of broken armor. Before I left, I went back to my father's grave once more. I'd laid his sword there when I buried him, the one he'd fought with at the end, and I stood over it a long moment before I picked it back up. He wouldn't need it where he was. I still might. The version of me that wanted adventure for fame and the gold, burned back in that village with everyone else. Ignatius found me again before I made it past the tree line, dropping down out of nowhere like he'd never actually left, and came with me anyway, bound to me somehow, through the scroll or something older, I don't know and I don't much care. I looked back at Innsvale once. There was nothing left to look back for. I just walked on.

But I remembered the eye. Somewhere out there he was still breathing, still giving orders like nothing had ever happened in Innsvale. I didn't know his name yet. I didn't need it. I'd know him the second I saw him again, and when I did, I was going to make sure he needed both eyes to see me coming.

* **Their Effluence (What form of emotional expression channels their magic?)**

He recites the poem “In the bleak midwinter…” either outloud, whispered or just movement of the lips  
The emotion he channels is grief/regret, he thinks about his parents and all the people in his village, he ran while they were being killed, and he will never forgive himself for it  
His magic isn't something he reaches for, it's something that surfaces when those memories and feelings come to the light

## **Backstory**

* **Personal Backstory (The full details of their past):**  
  **Lyon lost his mother shortly after he was born, his family was being hunted by other Vampires due the sins of his father, and they were actively on the run unfortunately they caught up to them and at that time the father was away due to some business and his mother had no choice but to hide Lyon somewhere safe to lure them away as he was just a baby, they eventually caught up to her and killed her she was fierce and fought back till her last breath but there was just too many of them, the father arrived too late but he did find some of them still wandering about the mansion looking for survivors, he killed every last one and found Lyon hidden under the wooden floorboards of the living room a crooked place for a baby but good enough to stay well hidden.**  
  **Years later when Lyon was about 15 years old his dad had become a very different person and Lyon found out the hard way when he discovered letters for his dad from a woman living in a nearby town apparently his dad has been keeping some very big secrets he had another child with a human woman and kept it from his son Lyon because he was too prideful in his Vampire blood and couldn’t bare the thought of his other child being mortal what they call a Dhampyr, Lyon was shocked finding out about this when he approached his dad and asked him the truth he quickly shut him down and forbade him to speak on the matter even threatening him.**   
  **Lyon swore to himself to find out the full truth about his sibling and the human mother, the letter stopped coming from her after a few months and he even went to the address to find them but they were nowhere to be seen he asked the townspeople about some woman with a child but no one seemed to know much and that she left a month ago and they hadn’t seen her since. Lyon assumed she was probably threatened in to leaving but he couldn’t yet chase after her as he was still only 15 and had his responsibilities to his father but as the years passed his drive to find his sibling grew greater and his father grew colder and more ruthless towards him and by the time he was 23 he was now fully educated on the world and the different languages and histories and how human societies really function, his father had drilled every mannerism and discipline in him by that point to prepare him for the human world even making assimilate with the people in town throughout the years, in a twisted way his father wanted him to be able to manipulate his way through human society since he was a vampire he had to learn and adapt except kindness he was mostly kind towards the humans not seeing them as prey unlike his father, which is exactly why he had no choice but to leave his father behind he traveled from town to town searching for his sibling all he knew was they had the same eyes and hair and that it was a boy, he kept his real identity hidden going by as a traveler, years passed he met a lot of people built a lot of connections and a reputation of sorts all to find his brother, he was 26 now still on the road still searching for his brother with only bits and pieces of information on his whereabouts, people had seen someone with red eyes and black hair travelling with an older woman but nothing more than that, the search continues with it being clear that they were constantly on the move not staying at one place for too long, but that was not going to stop Lyon.**  
    
* **Their Effluence (What form of emotional expression channels their magic?): Using blood as ink to draw magic symbols in mid air.**  
* **Motivation for Joining (Why are they adventuring with this specific group? Leave this till instructed to add): Most efficient way to find their Sibling is to travel with a well equipped and competent party.**

## **Group Dynamics**

* **Skills and Value to the Group (What role do they fill?): Sorcerer, knows offensive and defensive magic.**
